Cumulative risk of a first event by age

Source: R/agemix.R
cumrsk.Rd

The share of a birth cohort that has had a first arrest, conviction or prison admission by each age, from first events by age and the population: the hazard at each age is the first events over those still without one, and the cumulative risk is one minus the product of the complements, with Greenwood's interval on the log scale of the survival (Bonczar 2003; Pettit and Western 2004). With death rates the first events count only among the cohort still alive, and no interval is given.

Usage

cumrsk(age, ev, pop, atrisk = NULL, dth = NULL, level = 0.95)

Arguments

age

The ages, increasing.

ev

The first events at each age: numbers from 0.

pop

The population at each age: positive numbers.

atrisk

NULL (the population less those already with an event) or the number at risk at each age.

dth

NULL, or the death rate at each age, from 0 to below 1.

level

The level of the interval: one number between 0 and 1.

Value

A data frame of class cumrsk: age, hazard, atrisk, cumrisk, lo, hi (NA with death rates).

References

Pettit, B. and Western, B. (2004). Mass imprisonment and the life course: race and class inequality in U.S. incarceration. American Sociological Review, 69(2), 151-169. doi:10.1177/000312240406900201

Examples

cumrsk(18:22, c(120, 100, 80, 60, 40), rep(10000, 5))
#> cumrsk: cumulative risk of a first event by age
#>  age      hazard atrisk cumrisk          lo         hi
#>   18 0.012000000  10000   0.012 0.009863582 0.01413181
#>   19 0.010121457   9880   0.022 0.019120830 0.02487072
#>   20 0.008179959   9780   0.030 0.026650783 0.03333769
#>   21 0.006185567   9700   0.036 0.032341858 0.03964431
#>   22 0.004149378   9640   0.040 0.036151577 0.04383306
